what_its_for: Pramipexole is used to treat two conditions. First, it helps control the symptoms of Parkinson's disease, such as tremors (shaking), stiffness, and slow movement, by mimicking a natural chemical in your brain called dopamine. Second, it is used to treat Restless Legs Syndrome (RLS), a condition where you feel an uncomfortable urge to move your legs, especially at night.
how_to_take: Take pramipexole exactly as your doctor tells you. You can take it with or without food, but taking it with food may help if it upsets your stomach. Swallow extended-release tablets (Mirapex ER) whole — do not crush, chew, or split them. Regular tablets can be split if needed. Try to take your doses at the same times each day to keep a steady level of medicine in your body. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor first, as stopping too quickly can make your symptoms worse.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it over several weeks to find the dose that works best for you. For Parkinson's disease, the typical starting dose of the regular tablet is 0.125 mg taken three times a day. For Restless Legs Syndrome, a common starting dose is 0.125 mg taken once daily, 2 to 3 hours before bedtime. Your doctor will adjust your dose based on how well it works and how well you tolerate it. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as doses vary from person to person.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and just take your next regular dose on schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store pramipexole at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of any unused or expired medicine properly — ask your pharmacist about local drug take-back programs.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking pramipexole, as it can increase dizziness and drowsiness. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing anything that requires full alertness until you know how this medicine affects you, because it can cause sudden and extreme sleepiness. Be careful when standing up from a sitting or lying position, as pramipexole can cause dizziness or lightheadedness. Avoid taking other medicines that cause drowsiness without first talking to your doctor. Tell your doctor about all other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you are taking, as some can interact with pramipexole.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: sudden extreme drowsiness or falling asleep during daily activities; hallucinations (seeing or hearing things that are not there); confusion or unusual changes in mood or behavior; strong, unusual urges such as gambling, overeating, spending money, or increased sexual urges; fainting or severe dizziness; swelling in your legs or feet; or signs of a severe allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also call your doctor if your symptoms get worse or do not improve.
when_it_works: You may begin to notice some improvement in your symptoms within a few days to a couple of weeks, but it often takes several weeks of gradually increasing doses to feel the full benefit. Be patient and do not stop taking the medicine on your own if you do not feel better right away. Talk to your doctor if you have concerns about how the medicine is working.
special_populations: Kidney problems: If you have kidney disease, your doctor will likely prescribe a lower dose, since your body may clear the medicine more slowly than usual. Older adults: Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects such as hallucinations, confusion, and dizziness, so extra caution is needed. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of pramipexole during pregnancy and breastfeeding is not fully known, and your doctor will help you weigh the risks and benefits. Children: Pramipexole is not typically recommended for children, as its safety and effectiveness in patients under 18 have not been established.
